title: Cloudflare Makes Clairic Open-Weight, Adds Faster Clairic-flash
dek: Two data extraction models now read PDFs, with full weights on Hugging Face.

caption:
Cloudflare just open-sourced the weights to its data extraction AI. 🔓

The company released an updated 27-billion-parameter Clairic and a new, lighter 9B Clairic-flash. Both run on Workers AI, with full weights on Hugging Face. They pull clean, typed fields out of messy receipts, invoices, support tickets and documents, and now read PDFs too, up to four pages or images per request.

A rebuilt architecture generates every field in parallel, so Cloudflare says answers arrive in under a second with confidence scores and character spans attached. You only pay for input tokens: $0.10 per million, with the 27B model rising to $0.24 after December 1, 2026.

We at AI Parabellum see this as part of a bigger shift: small, purpose-built open-weight models replacing pricey LLM calls for narrow tasks. Just remember the accuracy numbers are Cloudflare's own, so test it on your data first.

post_caption:
Turning invoices and receipts into structured data no longer needs a giant chatbot. Cloudflare's Clairic and Clairic-flash are now open-weight, read PDFs, and respond in under a second.

The 27B Clairic costs the same as the 9B flash model until December 1, so now is the cheapest time to try it. 📄
